task.description:
WF-03 Step 4 -- REGRESSION TEST for ISS-0426. Both hard gates have PASSED (SECURITY-REVIEWER step-03b, REVIEWER step-03c). Read WF-03's Step 4 section for the fail-first rule, then read THIS description carefully, because ISS-0426 is an awkward fit for that rule and you must not apply it mechanically.

WHY THE STANDARD FAIL-FIRST SHAPE DOES NOT TRANSFER. WF-03 Step 4 normally requires a test that FAILS against pre-fix code and PASSES post-fix. ISS-0426's defect is a FLAKE: a wall-clock timeout that fires only under 6-way CPU contention on a 16-core host. ISSUE-FIXER could not reproduce it even with 24 OS-level CPU burners plus 48 concentrated runs of the affected test -- recorded in its Step 1 handoff as an honest negative. So a 'test that fails pre-fix' would be one that fails only probabilistically, on some hosts, sometimes. Writing one and claiming it demonstrates the fix would be exactly the speculation core-directives.md forbids. DO NOT fabricate a contention harness and assert it reproduces the flake unless you actually observe it reproducing.

WHAT TO PROVE INSTEAD -- the fix is STRUCTURAL, so prove it structurally. Design section 4 (read it) states the correctness is verifiable by construction rather than statistically: after the change, {:error, {:wallclock_timeout, _}} is UNREACHABLE from the 14 Group 1 call sites, because 11 no longer call Task.yield at all and 3 no longer evaluate any `after timeout_ms ->` clause. Your coverage should lock in THAT property so a future change reintroducing the race is caught. Properties worth locking (you decide the final shape):
  (a) The two new seams behave correctly: run_script_sync/3 and run_with_heap_limit_sync/4 return the same outcomes as their racing counterparts for the workloads Group 1 uses -- script_error, budget_exceeded, memory_limit_exceeded, :ok -- so the restructure did not change what the repointed tests assert. This is the highest-value coverage: 14 call sites were repointed to new code paths, and a subtly different return shape would let those tests pass for the wrong reason.
  (b) run_with_heap_limit_sync/4 still enforces the MEMORY limit -- max_heap_size kill:true is retained, so an over-allocating script still yields :memory_limit_exceeded. REQ-156/LUA-09's bound must be SHOWN intact through the new path, not assumed from the old.
  (c) The tag partition is wired correctly and the 11 :lua_wallclock_race tests still genuinely assert timeout behaviour -- i.e. they can still FAIL if the wall-clock kill regressed. A tagging fix's worst failure mode is tests excluded everywhere that therefore never fail again. Both reviewers confirmed they currently run (11 passed / 37 excluded isolated); consider whether anything should guard that wiring going forward.

WHERE FAIL-FIRST DOES APPLY, and how to satisfy it honestly. WF-03's own section 'When the pre-fix failure is the code under test does not exist' covers your case: the seams are NEW, so any test of them fails pre-fix with UndefinedFunctionError, which proves nothing about whether your tests discriminate a CORRECT seam from a WRONG one. That section therefore requires MUTATION: mutate the shipped logic and record which tests fail per mutant, targeting the specific traps the fix exists to handle. Suggested mutants (pick ones that actually probe your assertions): restore an `after timeout_ms ->` clause to run_with_heap_limit_sync/4 with a tiny timeout and confirm a test catches the reintroduced wallclock_timeout; drop the max_heap_size spawn_opt and confirm (b)'s memory test fails; make run_script_sync/3 delegate back to execute_with_manifest/3 and confirm something notices. Record pass/fail counts per mutant in your test spec.
  MUTANTS ARE TEMPORARY PROBES. WF-03 is explicit: leaving one in the tree is a step failure. Use a throwaway `git worktree` (preferred) or revert in place with `git checkout -- <path>` and VERIFY the revert -- quote BOTH `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` empty AND the test file re-running green -- in result.summary.

STANDING RULING FROM REVIEWER, follow rather than re-decide: the type checker emits a non-fatal 'clause will never match' note at executor_test.exs:466's `refute match?({:error, {:wallclock_timeout, _}}, result)`. REVIEWER ruled LEAVE IT AS-IS -- it is a standing, machine-checked proof that run_script_sync/3's categorical unreachability guarantee (design section 2.1.1b) holds; if a future change broke the guarantee the warning would silently DISAPPEAR, which is the signal worth preserving. It is CI-invisible (mix compile --warnings-as-errors only checks lib/). Do not remove or rewrite that assertion, and do NOT add more assertions of that shape elsewhere.

CONSTRAINTS: you own test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs only. Do NOT edit lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex except transiently for a mutant you then revert and verify. Do NOT touch the three wasm test files or lib/letflow/engine/wasm (owned by the live concurrent run WF03-ISS0418-20260902). Do NOT change production timeout semantics (AC4). You WRITE tests; TEST-RUNNER owns the full-suite gate -- but run your own new tests to confirm they pass, and you must run the mutants.

Complete the handoff with your test spec (including the per-mutant results table), real quoted output, and the revert verification. Commit and push to branch feature/WF03-ISS0426-20260902. next_action: 'Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR'.

result.summary:
TEST-DESIGNER wrote 8 new tests in 3 describe blocks appended to test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs (282 insertions, 0 deletions -- no existing test modified beyond ELIXIR-DEV's already-gated repointing), plus the spec at test/specs/ISS-0426.md. Coverage follows the handoff's three properties rather than a fabricated contention harness, because the filed flake is not reproducible on demand (ISSUE-FIXER's Step 1 negative result): (a) seam equivalence -- 4 tests proving run_script_sync/3 and run_with_heap_limit_sync/4 return outcomes identical to their racing execute_with_manifest/3 counterparts across all four outcome shapes (:ok, budget_exceeded, script_error, memory_limit_exceeded), which is the highest-value coverage since 14 call sites were repointed onto new code paths; (b) the memory limit still binds through the unbounded-wait seam -- same script, small limit yields :memory_limit_exceeded, large limit yields :ok, so REQ-156/LUA-09's bound is shown intact through the new path rather than assumed from the old; (c) tag-partition integrity -- an AST-based exact-count check that exactly 11 tests carry :lua_wallclock_race (using Code.string_to_quoted/1 as in tenant_slug_test.exs's ISS-0065 regression test, because a naive grep over-counts to 15 against the block's own prose), an AST check that test_helper.exs excludes the tag, and a live subprocess run asserting the isolated partition still passes exactly 11.

FAIL-FIRST VIA MUTATION, per WF-03's 'when the pre-fix failure is the code under test does not exist' section -- the seams are new, so UndefinedFunctionError would prove nothing. Four mutants applied in a THROWAWAY git worktree with independent deps/_build (the real working tree's lib/ was never mutated), each producing a DISCRIMINATING failure set rather than blanket breakage:
  1. Restore an `after` clause (1ms) to run_with_heap_limit_sync/4 -> 4/45 failed (REQ-156 AC-1, AC-2, property-(a) test 4, property-(b) test 1).
  2. Drop the max_heap_size spawn_opt -> 4/45 failed (same 4 tests, reached via :ok instead of the expected limit).
  3. Force run_script_sync/3 through a deterministic reintroduced wallclock-timeout path -> 12/45 failed (every run_script_sync/3 caller, including property-(a) tests 1-3).
  4. Drop :lua_wallclock_race from test_helper.exs's exclude list -> 1/56 failed (property-(c) test 2 only).
Each mutant was reverted before the next was applied.

REVERT VERIFICATION (ORCH re-verified independently after the agent's session ended): `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` shows ONLY the intended test/ changes (M test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs, A test/specs/ISS-0426.md) -- no lib/ entry, so no mutant residue. `git diff HEAD --stat -- lib/` is EMPTY, i.e. lib/ is byte-identical to the reviewed commit. `git diff main...HEAD --numstat -- lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex` still reads 113 insertions / 0 deletions, so AC4 holds unchanged. The mutation worktree is gone from `git worktree list`.

SELF-CAUGHT ERROR, reported rather than hidden: an early draft duplicated the REVIEWER-blessed 'clause will never match' assertion shape at a second site, violating REVIEWER's standing ruling not to add more assertions of that shape. TEST-DESIGNER detected this by actually running the file and removed it before finalising.

VERIFICATION QUOTED (the two partition runs were re-run by ORCH after the agent's session ended, on the same tree):
  mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs
    -> Finished in 7.4 seconds (7.4s async, 0.00s sync) / Result: 45 passed, 11 excluded
  mix test --only lua_wallclock_race test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs
    -> Finished in 3.9 seconds (3.9s async, 0.00s sync) / Result: 11 passed, 45 excluded
  Complementary at 56 total (48 pre-existing + 8 new), confirming the new tests run in the default partition and the 11 tagged tests still execute in isolation.
  TEST-DESIGNER also confirmed `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors` clean and `mix format --check-formatted` clean.

NOT YET ESTABLISHED AT THE TIME OF THIS WRITE: the full-suite serial gate. TEST-DESIGNER declined to fabricate it and its session ended while that background run was still going; ORCH has re-launched `mix test` and will record the real result at TEST-RUNNER's step, which owns the full-suite gate in any case. ELIXIR-DEV's own pre-test-addition full serial run measured 3049 passed / 0 failures, which is the baseline this must be compared against -- it is NOT a substitute for the post-test run.

issues.description: TEST-DESIGNER's session ended before it could commit its own handoff and before its background full-suite run reported. ORCH completed the handoff record from the agent's reported results, re-verified the revert and both partition runs first-hand rather than inheriting them, and explicitly left the full-suite result unrecorded rather than assuming it. No work was lost -- the test code and spec were already written to the tree.
